chapter.name: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

subtopics.name: Acidic and Basic Strength of Organic Compounds

questions.stem:
The correct order of increasing basic strength of the following amines in aqueous solution is:
(I) $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$
(II) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH}$
(III) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}$
(IV) $\mathrm{NH_3}$
questions.solution: For methyl-substituted amines in aqueous medium, the order of basic strength is governed by inductive effect, steric hindrance, and solvation. The experimentally determined order of basicity is: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > \mathrm{(CH_3)_3N} > \mathrm{NH_3}$. Thus, $\text{IV} < \text{III} < \text{I} < \text{II}$.

questions.stem:
Among the following compounds, the total number of compounds which are more acidic than phenol is ________.
Propan-1-ol, $o$-Nitrophenol, $m$-Nitrophenol, $p$-Nitrophenol, Ethanol, $o$-Cresol
questions.solution:
Acidic strength of nitro-substituted phenols is higher than phenol because of the electron-withdrawing $-\text{I}$ and $-\text{M}$ effects of the $-\text{NO}_2$ group.
Thus, $o$-nitrophenol, $m$-nitrophenol, and $p$-nitrophenol are all more acidic than phenol.
Propan-1-ol and ethanol are weaker acids than phenol because phenoxide ion is resonance stabilized.
$o$-Cresol is less acidic due to the electron-donating methyl group ($+\text{I}$ and hyperconjugation).
Therefore, there are exactly 3 compounds more acidic than phenol.

questions.stem:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of basic strength:
(I) Aniline
(II) $p$-Nitroaniline
(III) $p$-Toluidine
(IV) $p$-Anisidine
questions.solution:
Basic strength depends on electron density on the nitrogen. 
- $-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ group (in $p$-anisidine) is highly electron donating via $+M$ effect (strongest base).
- $-\mathrm{CH_3}$ group (in $p$-toluidine) is electron donating via $+I$ and hyperconjugation.
- Aniline is unsubstituted.
- $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ group (in $p$-nitroaniline) is strongly electron-withdrawing via $-M$ and $-I$ (weakest base).
Thus, the correct order is IV > III > I > II.
